macro.regime: Waller's dovish pivot drives a second straight rally, but a live Hormuz war and Friday's NFP keep the path genuinely two-sided
macro.narrative: Thursday 3 Sep extended Wednesday's rebound into a second straight strong rally: the S&P 500 rose 1.06% to 7747.71 (Nasdaq +1.40%, Dow +1.18%, Russell 2000 +0.51%), with VIX falling a further 5.79% to 14.32. The specific driver was Fed Governor Christopher Waller's dovish pre-market remarks (8:30am ET) that he could back a September rate hold 'so long as upcoming inflation data doesn't produce surprises' -- pulling implied September-hike odds from roughly 63% to 50% and nudging the 10y yield down to ~4.77%. Rate-sensitive names led (Oracle +5.7%, Palantir +7.7%, financials broadly higher). Gold, silver and miners extended their rally for a second day (GLD +1.85% to $410.22, SLV +2.51% to $60.55, GDX +3.95%, SILJ +2.37%, NEM +4.21%) with silver holding above $66/oz (+60.8% y/y) -- but Barrick Gold (GOLD) fell 5.34% to $41.48 on company-specific news: Bloomberg reported 2 Sep that Barrick is weighing delaying its North America gold-unit IPO from 2026 to 2027 amid a shareholder revolt against Chairman John Thornton's separation strategy, a governance story that does not read through to the rest of the miners complex. The Hormuz/Iran conflict remains live: the US struck two Iranian government tankers plus roughly 100 IRGC-linked air-defense/radar/drone sites on 2 Sep, Iran retaliated with missiles and drones against Gulf bases (mostly intercepted over Jordan/Bahrain), and Strait of Hormuz transits have collapsed to single digits per 24 hours from a pre-crisis pace near 138/day -- even as Trump publicly downplayed further escalation, calling the strikes 'brief.' Oil is on track for its biggest weekly gain since July (WTI near $92, Brent near $95) though the rally has cooled slightly on Trump's de-escalatory framing. Crypto rebounded sharply -- BTC +4.96% to ~$81,138 on a ~$415M short squeeze and renewed spot-ETF inflows (+$100M net 2 Sep) -- even as the Sep 15 CLARITY Act Senate cloture-vote passage odds deteriorated further to roughly 19.5% (down from a 58% high in August and ~30% just a week ago), with 8 Democratic votes still needed and uncommitted, a hardening near-term regulatory tail risk for the crypto sleeve specifically. Asia partially caught up to the US rally: the Hang Seng rose 0.6% to 25,459 Thursday (Tencent +0.4%, reversing about a third of Wednesday's -1.19% lag), while Xiaomi remains under pressure (-2.21% Wed) on investor concern about EV/IoT margin sustainability ahead of its September product blitz (Xiaomi 18 series, SkyNomad EV, YU7 GT). Today (Friday 4 Sep, 20:30 SGT) brings the single most important scheduled print of the week -- US Non-Farm Payrolls (cons 55K vs -23K prior, unemployment cons 4.1%) -- the last major data point before the Sep 15-16 FOMC; a hot print with wages above 0.3% would revive the hike odds Waller just cooled. The Sep 15 CLARITY Act cloture-vote passage odds have deteriorated further to ~19.5% (from a 58% August high, and down from ~30% just a week ago) with 8 Democratic votes still needed -- a hardening, not fading, regulatory tail risk.
Waller's dovish pivot and the pullback in the 10y yield are a broad risk-on tailwind that lifted BTC alongside equities and gold Thursday.
Genuinely stacked binary-catalyst week ahead (Sep 15 CLARITY vote + Sep 15-16 FOMC) keeps near-term volatility elevated in both directions.

calls.name: Ethereum
drivers: ETH rebounded alongside BTC on Thursday's broad risk-on move (Waller-driven equity/gold/crypto rally), reversing part of Tuesday's Iran-driven selloff.
August's ETH-ETF-inflow-over-BTC rotation signal (from the prior run) remains a supportive structural undercurrent independent of this week's news.
Exposed to the same hardening Sep 15 CLARITY Act binary as BTC (odds now ~19.5%, down further from 58%) landing the same week as the FOMC.
No ETH-specific catalyst found fresh this run; view is macro-inferred from the broader crypto correlation to Thursday's rally.

calls.name: Solana
drivers: SOL rebounded alongside BTC/ETH on Thursday's broad risk-on move, its typically highest-beta profile amplifying both the Tuesday selloff and Thursday's recovery.
Exposed to the same hardening Sep 15 CLARITY Act binary as the rest of the crypto sleeve (odds now ~19.5%, down further from 58%).
Less institutional/ETF support than BTC or ETH implies larger swings in both directions into the stacked Sep 15/15-16 FOMC-and-CLARITY-vote week.
No SOL-specific catalyst found fresh this run; view is macro-inferred from the broader crypto correlation.

calls.name: iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF
drivers: Waller's dovish pivot pulled the 10y yield down to ~4.77% from ~4.81%, a direct near-term tailwind for long-duration Treasury prices after weeks of hawkish-repricing pressure.
September-hike odds fell from ~63% to ~50% on Waller's remarks -- the sharpest dovish move in weeks, though still a coin-flip outcome.
Friday's NFP is the key swing factor: a hot print with wages above 0.3% would revive hike odds and reverse this week's yield relief quickly.
Sticky underlying inflation data (still the dominant multi-week theme) means this is a tactical relief, not a confirmed trend reversal, pending confirmation into the Sep 15-16 FOMC.

calls.name: iShares 7-10 Year Treasury Bond ETF
drivers: Less duration risk than TLT but still benefits from Waller's dovish pivot pulling the 10y yield down to ~4.77%.
Same NFP-week swing-factor setup as TLT, just with lower magnitude of price impact given shorter duration.
September-hike odds falling to ~50% from ~63% is a genuine, if tentative, easing of the hawkish-repricing headwind.
Two-sided into the Sep 15-16 FOMC pending Friday's payrolls confirmation.

calls.name: iShares 1-3 Year Treasury Bond ETF
drivers: Least duration-sensitive of the Treasury ladder, so least exposed to this week's yield swings in either direction.
Front-end yields easing modestly on Waller's dovish pivot, though carry/coupon dominates the return profile at this maturity regardless.
A relatively low-volatility parking spot into the NFP-and-FOMC-heavy stretch ahead.
Directly benefits from cash/short-duration remaining attractive amid the still genuinely two-sided Fed path.

calls.name: iShares TIPS Bond ETF
drivers: ISM Prices Paid stuck at 71.1% for a second month (23rd consecutive month of rising input costs) supports inflation breakevens.
Oil spike (WTI +5.81%) adds a fresh near-term inflation-expectations tailwind that pure nominal bonds don't capture.
Rising real yields from the hawkish Fed repricing are a price headwind that partially offsets the breakeven support.
CPI 3.4% y/y (July) with the next print due Sep 11 is the key near-term catalyst for the inflation-protection thesis.

calls.name: iShares iBoxx Investment Grade Corporate Bond ETF
drivers: IG spreads remain tight at ~78bp and essentially unchanged in August despite AI-funding questions and Mideast tension -- credit-specific risk is low.
Duration risk from the hawkish rate repricing (10y ~4.81%) is the dominant headwind for LQD price, overwhelming the tight-spread support.
Strong corporate earnings this quarter have helped keep spreads resilient, a genuine fundamental support.
Net effect is duration-driven negative near-term with spread stability providing a floor versus a genuine credit-stress scenario.

calls.name: iShares iBoxx High Yield Corporate Bond ETF
drivers: HY spreads tightened 19bp in August, the sector's strongest month of the year despite typically being the second-worst seasonally.
Shorter effective duration than IG/Treasuries means less price impact from the hawkish rate repricing specifically.
Energy-sector HY issuers benefit directly from the WTI +5.81% spike given HY's typically higher energy-sector weighting.
Strong corporate earnings and favorable supply/demand technicals continue to support spread resilience per market commentary.

calls.name: iShares JP Morgan USD Emerging Markets Bond ETF
drivers: Dollar strength (DXY ~99.5-99.7 post-Jackson Hole) is a direct headwind for USD-denominated EM debt via issuer funding costs.
Higher US rates (57-72% hike odds) generally tighten global dollar-funding conditions for EM sovereigns.
Oil-importing EM sovereigns face an added terms-of-trade headwind from the Hormuz-driven oil spike; oil exporters within the index benefit.
No EMB-specific fresh catalyst found this run; view is macro-inferred.

calls.name: Vanguard Total Bond Market ETF
drivers: Blended Treasury/IG-credit duration exposure means BND inherits the same hawkish-rate-repricing headwind as TLT/IEF/LQD, just diluted.
10y yield at 4.81% (highest since Jan 2025) is the dominant driver of the near-term price headwind.
IG credit-spread resilience (78bp, tight and stable) provides a partial offset versus a pure-duration play.
Softening labor data (JOLTS, ISM Manufacturing) into Friday's NFP is the key swing factor that could reverse the rate-repricing headwind.

callsNote: Research-only deliverable produced 2026-09-04 (SGT) against the actual Thu 3 Sep US close (S&P 500 7,747.71 +1.06%, Nasdaq 26,584.06 +1.40%, Dow 53,686.11 +1.18%, Russell 2000 2,968.27 +0.51%, VIX 14.32 -5.79%). Thursday's rally was driven specifically by Fed Governor Waller's dovish pre-market remarks (8:30am ET) that he could back a September hold absent an inflation surprise, pulling hike odds from ~63% to ~50% and the 10y yield to ~4.77%. Gold/silver/miners extended their rally for a second day (GLD +1.85%, SLV +2.51%, GDX +3.95%, NEM +4.21%) except Barrick Gold (-5.34%), confirmed as a company-specific IPO-delay/governance story (Bloomberg, 2 Sep) rather than a gold-market signal -- every other tracked miner rallied the same session. The Hormuz/Iran conflict remains live (US struck two Iranian tankers plus ~100 IRGC-linked sites 2 Sep; Iran retaliated with missiles/drones on Gulf bases; Strait transits collapsed to single digits/24h) even as Trump downplayed further escalation. BTC rebounded +4.96% to ~$81,138 on a short squeeze and renewed ETF inflows even as the Sep 15 CLARITY Act cloture-vote odds deteriorated further to ~19.5% (from a 58% high). Friday's NFP (cons 55K vs -23K prior, 20:30 SGT) is the pivotal swing print into the Sep 15-16 FOMC and has not yet happened as of this research. Breadth and credit-spread figures fresher than Tuesday 1 Sep's verified readings could not be independently confirmed this run (search results returned internally inconsistent session closes and at least one likely-hallucinated sector-breakdown claim, both discarded rather than published) and are carried forward. Tickers with genuine fresh news this run (SPY, QQQ, IWM, GLD, SLV, DBC, USO, BTC-USD, ETH-USD, SOL-USD, TLT, IEF, SHY, XLF) received updated drivers; all other calls are carried forward from the 3 Sep run with unchanged priors rather than fabricated updates.
